threads.body: The idea is that since static initialization of `SpringWebTelemetryBuilder` calls `setBuilderExtractor` it is impossible to create and instance of `SpringWebTelemetryBuilder` so that the `builderExtractor` would be `null`.

replies.body:
added comments

the reason I prefer this compared to using `@Initializer` is that there's no enforcement of `@Initializer`, so it's basically just a suppression mechanism
I added `requireNonNull()` to make it clearer

threads.body: The comment says the extractor is "guaranteed non-null", but the implementation silently skips configuration when it is null. This changes behavior compared to the previous approach (which would fail fast) and could hide classloading/initialization issues, resulting in builders not being configured from OpenTelemetry properties. Consider either (a) removing the null-check and failing fast with a clear exception/message, or (b) adjusting the comment to reflect that config application is best-effort and intentionally optional.

This method claims the extractor is guaranteed to be set, but still guards with `if (builderExtractor != null)` and otherwise does nothing. If the extractor is unexpectedly null, the server builder will not be configured from OpenTelemetry properties and the failure will be silent. Consider failing fast (e.g., `requireNonNull(builderExtractor, ...)`) or updating the comment to match the intended optional behavior.

`applyClientCommonConfig` silently does nothing if `clientBuilderExtractor` is null, even though the comment says it is guaranteed to be initialized. If null ever occurs, client instrumentation will miss common configuration without any signal. Consider failing fast with a clear exception/message, or revise the comment to reflect intentional best-effort behavior.

Same as the client variant: `applyServerCommonConfig` silently skips configuration when `serverBuilderExtractor` is null, which contradicts the "guaranteed" comment and could hide initialization/classloading issues. Consider failing fast or updating the comment to match the intended behavior.

The comment says the extractor is guaranteed to be set during builder class initialization, but the method currently treats it as optional and silently skips config when it is null. If this ever happens, the interceptor will be built without applying common OpenTelemetry configuration. Consider failing fast with a clear message, or adjust the comment to reflect intentional best-effort behavior.
